description.en-US: Cross-session memory: write / read / list / search / delete (writes undoable)
description.zh-CN: 跨会话持久记忆：写 / 读 / 列举 / 搜索 / 删除（写入可机械撤销）

tools.description: Store a value under a key in the persistent memory (survives across sessions). Args: key (required, unique identifier), value (required, text), tags (optional, short label), type (optional: "user" | "feedback" | "project" | "reference" — it decides which layer the entry lands in by default: "user" / "feedback" are global preferences that apply in every project, "project" / "reference" stay in the current project), scope (optional override: "project" | "global"; wins over the type default). A "feedback" or "project" entry should carry two lines in the value — `Why:` (the reason, which is what makes edge cases judgeable) and `How to apply:` — a missing one comes back as `hint` but is still written. Overwrites any existing value; the overwritten entry is returned in `previous` and can be restored via memory_undo. Project entries are scoped to the current project: the same key in another project holds a different value. An unassociated session cannot write project memories (associate a project first, or pass type="user" / scope="global"). Use it for facts, decisions and user preferences worth remembering; do NOT store secrets or large blobs.
tools.name: memory_write

key.description: unique identifier, max 512 bytes; use dotted namespaces like `user.language`

scope.description: explicit layer override; wins over the type default

type.description: what kind of memory this is; decides the default layer (see scope)

tools.description: Read one memory entry by exact key. Looks in the current project first, then falls back to global user preferences. Returns {found, key, value, tags, updated_at, scope: "project"|"global"}; found=false when absent from both. Use on demand when the request touches prior context — not as an opening step.
tools.name: memory_read

tools.description: List memory entries of the current project plus global user preferences, ordered by key; each entry carries scope ("project"|"global"). Args: prefix (optional key-prefix filter), limit (default 50, max 200), offset (default 0). Returns {total, entries: [{key, value, tags, updated_at, scope}]} where total counts ALL matching entries.
tools.name: memory_list

tools.description: Substring search across keys, values and tags of the current project plus global user preferences (ASCII case-insensitive). Args: query (required), limit (default 20, max 100). Returns {query, matches: [{key, value, tags, updated_at, scope}]} — scope tells project records from global preferences. Wildcards in the query are matched literally. Use on demand when the request touches prior context — not as an opening step.
tools.name: memory_search

query.description: substring to search for; % and _ are literal

tools.description: Delete one memory entry by exact key from the CURRENT project scope only. Global user preferences cannot be deleted here — they are managed from the human memory management page. The deleted entry is returned in `previous_entry` and can be restored via memory_undo; deleting a missing key is a no-op.
tools.name: memory_delete

tools.description: Undo a previous memory_write or memory_delete by restoring the entry captured in its result. Can be invoked directly after a mistaken write/delete. Args mirror the compensation payload {call_id, args, output}; only output.previous (for write) or output.previous_entry (for delete) is used. Restoring overwrites the entry's current content with the old value — classified Irreversible, so approval follows the session's permission mode (asked by default, auto-approved in full-access mode).
tools.name: memory_undo

call_id.description: id of the original memory_write / memory_delete call

output.description: original call result carrying previous or previous_entry
